ashwini-nakshatra.description: Ashwini nakshatra explained: the Ashwini Kumaras and Ketu, the horse's head, the healing temple at Thiruthuraipoondi, and simple poojas for the star.
outline: Hook: The first star of the zodiac belongs to two horse-headed physicians who arrive at dawn, and the story of how they healed an old sage tells you most of what tradition says about Ashwini.

## Who rules Ashwini nakshatra, and why a horse's head? — the Ashwini Kumaras as its deities and Ketu as adhipati; the horse as speed, arrival and the first light; tradition's picture of Ashwini-born people as quick starters with a healer's instinct, offered as description, not destiny

## The twins who made an old man young — the Mahabharata and Shatapatha Brahmana tale of the sage Chyavana and Sukanya: the twins restore his youth in a pool, and in gratitude he wins them a share of soma the gods had refused; the story is really about healing earning its place at the table

## Where do Ashwini-born devotees go to pray? — the Piravi Marundeeswarar temple at Thiruthuraipoondi, traditionally associated with the star, whose name means the Lord who is medicine for birth itself; monthly star-day archana, a lamp on the janma nakshatra, Dhanvantari worship as a natural companion; the yearly star birthday in the birth month as a day for a visit or an archana
Close: On your star day, do one small healing thing for someone else: a call to a sick relative, a meal, a doctor's appointment you have been putting off. That is the Ashwini way of keeping the star.
takeaways: Ashwini is the first of the 27 nakshatras, presided over by the Ashwini Kumaras, the divine physician twins, with Ketu as its ruling planet.
The Piravi Marundeeswarar temple at Thiruthuraipoondi in Tamil Nadu is traditionally associated with Ashwini nakshatra.
Tradition links the star with healing and fresh starts; the simplest observance is a lamp and a prayer on your monthly star day.

faq.q: Which temple is associated with Ashwini nakshatra?
faq.a: The widely cited Tamil list of nakshatra temples names the Piravi Marundeeswarar temple at Thiruthuraipoondi, in Tiruvarur district, as the Ashwini nakshatra temple. The name means the Lord who is the medicine for birth, fitting a star ruled by divine physicians. Devotees often offer archana there on their star day, or arrange one from afar when travel is not possible.

faq.q: Who are the Ashwini Kumaras?
faq.a: The Ashwini Kumaras are twin gods of the Rig Veda, physicians to the gods, pictured with horses' heads or riding a golden chariot at dawn. They rescue sailors, restore sight and heal the sick in many hymns. The best-known Ashwini Kumaras story tells how they gave youth back to the aged sage Chyavana and earned a share of soma.

faq.q: What are Aswini star characteristics according to tradition?
faq.a: Traditional texts describe people born under Aswini, the Tamil spelling, as quick, eager to begin, independent and drawn to helping or healing others. Some add impatience as the shadow side. These are tradition's descriptions of a star's temperament, not predictions; a full chart and a person's own choices shape a life far more than one star.

faq.q: What pooja is good for Ashwini nakshatra?
faq.a: Many families light a lamp and offer archana to Shiva on the monthly Ashwini star day, and some add prayers to Dhanvantari, the physician form of Vishnu, because of the star's healing theme. Ketu, the ruling planet, is traditionally honoured through Ganesha worship. Keep it simple and regular rather than elaborate and occasional.

bharani-nakshatra.description: Bharani nakshatra as a practice: Yama and Shukra, the symbol of the womb, the Nalladai temple, and one week of restraint to try on your star day.
outline: Hook: Bharani is ruled by Yama, and most people flinch at the name; try reading Yama as the god of limits instead of the god of endings, and the star starts to make sense.

## Why does a star ruled by Yama feel like renewal? — Yama as presiding deity and Shukra as adhipati; the yoni, the womb, as the star's symbol, holding restraint and creation together; tradition describes Bharani-born people as intense, loyal and able to carry heavy things, a description rather than a sentence

## What Nachiketa learned from Bharani nakshatra's god — in the Katha Upanishad, the boy Nachiketa waits three days at Yama's door without food and refuses every pleasure Yama offers until he gets his real answer; the practice underneath is restraint as a way of choosing

## A Bharani week: temple, star day, one limit — the Agneeswarar temple at Nalladai, near Mayiladuthurai, traditionally associated with the star; a lamp on the janma nakshatra day each month; Durga worship on Tuesdays and Fridays, which many Bharani families keep; once a year, the star birthday in your birth month, kept quietly
Close: Try this for a week: pick one small limit, no phone at the table, no second helping, and keep it without announcing it. Notice what gets clearer.
takeaways: Bharani nakshatra is presided over by Yama, the god of dharma and limits, with Shukra as its ruling planet and the womb as its symbol.
The Agneeswarar temple at Nalladai in Tamil Nadu is traditionally associated with Bharani, and many devotees also pray to Durga.
Read through practice, Bharani is about restraint that makes room for something new, not about fear of endings.

faq.q: Is Bharani nakshatra bad or inauspicious?
faq.a: No. Yama as the presiding deity makes some people nervous, but in the tradition Yama is also Dharmaraja, the keeper of right order, and the one who teaches Nachiketa in the Katha Upanishad. Bharani is paired with Shukra, the planet of beauty and creativity. Folk sayings about any star are best held lightly; no star is a verdict on a person.

faq.q: Which temple is associated with Bharani nakshatra?
faq.a: The widely cited Tamil list of nakshatra temples names the Agneeswarar temple at Nalladai, near Mayiladuthurai in Tamil Nadu, as the Bharani nakshatra temple. Devotees born under the star often visit on their janma nakshatra day, the day each month when the Moon returns to Bharani, or arrange an archana there from a distance when travel is not practical.

faq.q: What are Bharani star characteristics in Jyotish?
faq.a: Traditional descriptions of Bharani star characteristics include intensity, loyalty, strong appetites, creativity and the capacity to bear responsibility. The womb as a symbol suggests someone who holds and carries things until they are ready. Treat these as tradition's portrait of a star rather than facts about you; the full chart and your own choices matter more.

krittika-nakshatra.description: Krittika nakshatra, Karthigai in Tamil: Agni and Surya, the razor-sharp flame, the six mothers of Murugan, and the Kanjanagaram temple for the star.
outline: Hook: On the Edison train one morning a colleague asked why my phone reminder said 'Karthigai' every month; I had kept that star day for years, a habit from home, without ever explaining it.

## Krittika nakshatra: fire, the Sun and a blade — Agni as presiding deity and Surya as adhipati; the razor or flame as symbol, the star that cuts and cooks; tradition describes Karthigai-born people as sharp, direct, protective and quick to purify, a portrait rather than a prediction

## Why is Murugan so tied to Karthigai? — the Skanda Purana story of the six sparks from Shiva's eye, the six babies in the Saravana pool, and the six Krittika sisters who nursed them until Parvati gathered them into one child with six faces; the monthly Karthigai day as Murugan's day, with one line from the Kanda Sashti Kavacham

## Temple, star day and a small observance — the Kathra Sundareswarar temple at Kanjanagaram, near Mayiladuthurai, traditionally associated with the star; a lamp on the monthly Karthigai day; Palani and the six abodes as the Murugan temples Karthigai families often hold close; the yearly Karthigai star birthday in the birth month, which many families keep in place of the calendar date
Close: One small thing for this week: on the next Karthigai day, light one lamp before breakfast and say Murugan's name six times, once for each of the mothers who fed him.
takeaways: Krittika, called Karthigai in Tamil, is presided over by Agni with Surya as its ruling planet; its symbol is a razor or flame.
The six Krittika sisters nursed the infant Murugan in the Skanda Purana, which is why the monthly Karthigai star day is kept for Murugan.
The Kathra Sundareswarar temple at Kanjanagaram is traditionally associated with Krittika nakshatra.

faq.q: Which temple is the Karthigai nakshatra temple?
faq.a: The widely cited Tamil list of nakshatra temples names the Kathra Sundareswarar temple at Kanjanagaram, near Mayiladuthurai, as the temple traditionally associated with Karthigai, the Tamil name for Krittika. Many Karthigai-born devotees also keep a bond with Murugan temples such as Palani, because the six Krittika sisters are remembered as the foster mothers of Murugan in the Skanda Purana.

faq.q: Why is the Karthigai star day important for Murugan devotees?
faq.a: In the Skanda Purana, six sparks from Shiva became six babies in the Saravana pool, and the six Krittika sisters nursed them. Murugan is therefore called Karthikeya, son of the Krittikas. Each month, when the Moon passes through Karthigai, devotees light lamps, fast lightly or visit a Murugan temple. The larger Karthigai Deepam festival grows from the same star.

faq.q: What are the qualities of Krittika nakshatra people?
faq.a: Tradition pictures Krittika-born people as sharp, honest to the point of bluntness, protective of those in their care, and strongly driven by standards. The flame symbol suggests both warmth and a capacity to burn. Jyotish offers these as tendencies associated with the star, not fixed traits; the rest of the chart and personal effort matter far more.

rohini-nakshatra.description: Rohini nakshatra, Krishna's birth star: Brahma and Chandra, the cart, why the Moon loved Rohini best, and the Pandava Thoodha Perumal temple link.
outline: Hook: The Moon married twenty-seven sisters and loved only one of them, Rohini; that favouritism, and the curse it earned, is the oldest story about this star, and it is really a story about attention.

## Why did the Moon love Rohini best? — Brahma (Prajapati) as presiding deity and Chandra as adhipati; the Puranic tale of Daksha's daughters, Chandra lingering in Rohini's house, Daksha's curse of wasting and the waxing and waning that followed; Rohini as the Moon's exalted home in Jyotish

## Rohini nakshatra and the child born at midnight — the Bhagavata Purana places Krishna's birth on the eighth day of the waning moon with the Moon in Rohini; the cart or chariot as the star's symbol, carrying growth and abundance; tradition describes Rohini-born people as charming, steady, fond of beauty and comfort

## A messenger's temple for a cowherd's star — the Pandava Thoodha Perumal temple in Kanchipuram, where Krishna stands as the envoy of the Pandavas, traditionally associated with Rohini; the monthly star day as a day for Krishna archana, a little butter and tulsi; the yearly star birthday in the birth month as a family occasion
Close: The Moon's curse was for not sharing its attention fairly. On your Rohini day, give an hour of undivided attention to someone who rarely gets it; the star is best kept that way.
takeaways: Rohini nakshatra is presided over by Brahma as Prajapati, ruled by Chandra, and symbolised by a cart; it is the Moon's favourite star in the Puranas.
The Bhagavata Purana places Krishna's birth under Rohini, which is why Rohini is widely known as Krishna's birth star.
The Pandava Thoodha Perumal temple in Kanchipuram is traditionally associated with Rohini nakshatra.

faq.q: Is Rohini really Krishna's birth star?
faq.a: Yes, in the tradition. The Bhagavata Purana and later texts describe Krishna being born at midnight on the eighth day of the waning moon, with the Moon in Rohini. In some years Ashtami and Rohini do not coincide exactly, so communities differ on which to follow for Janmashtami. That is why families ask each season whether to follow the star or the lunar day.

faq.q: Which temple is associated with Rohini nakshatra?
faq.a: The widely cited Tamil list of nakshatra temples names the Pandava Thoodha Perumal temple in Kanchipuram as the Rohini nakshatra temple. Here Vishnu is worshipped as Krishna the envoy, who went to the Kaurava court seeking peace for the Pandavas. Rohini-born devotees often offer archana there on their star day or arrange one from afar.

faq.q: What are Rohini star characteristics in astrology?
faq.a: Tradition describes Rohini-born people as attractive, artistic, affectionate, steady and fond of comfort and good food, with possessiveness as the shadow side. Since Rohini is the Moon's exalted star, emotional sensitivity is often mentioned. These are traditional tendencies linked to a star, not certainties; the whole chart and personal choices shape temperament far more.

mrigashira-nakshatra.description: Mrigashira nakshatra as a practice: Soma and Mangal, the deer's head, the seeker's restless mind, the Enkan temple, and a week of curious attention.
outline: Hook: Watch a deer at the edge of a field: head up, ears turning, ready to move at any sound. Mrigashira's symbol is that head, and the star is about searching well rather than searching endlessly.

## What was the deer running from? — the Aitareya Brahmana image of Prajapati pursuing his daughter as a deer across the sky and Rudra's arrow stopping him, read in the sky as Orion's belt; for practice, the lesson is to notice when seeking turns into chasing

## Temple, star day and a Murugan connection — the Adhi Narayana Perumal temple at Enkan, near Tiruvarur, traditionally associated with the star; a lamp and a quiet sitting on the monthly janma nakshatra day; Murugan worship, which many families keep because Mangal rules the star; the yearly star birthday in the birth month as a day for a temple visit

takeaways: Mrigashira nakshatra is presided over by Soma, ruled by Mangal (Mars), and symbolised by a deer's head, the image of an alert seeker.
The Adhi Narayana Perumal temple at Enkan in Tamil Nadu is traditionally associated with Mrigashira, called Mirugaseeridam in Tamil.
The star's practice is curiosity with attention: seek, but notice when seeking turns into chasing.

faq.q: What is the Tamil name for Mrigashira and its temple?

The widely cited Tamil list of nakshatra temples names the Adhi Narayana Perumal temple at Enkan, in Tiruvarur district, as the temple traditionally associated with it. Devotees born under the Mirugaseeridam star often visit on their star day or offer archana there from afar.

faq.q: What are Mrigashira nakshatra characteristics?
faq.a: Tradition describes Mrigashira-born people as curious, gentle, intelligent, fond of travel and conversation, and sometimes restless or unsure where to settle. Jyotish treats these as tendencies associated with the star rather than fixed traits, and the rest of the birth chart changes the picture considerably.

faq.a: Soma, the Moon's nectar, is the star's presiding deity, so Monday prayers to Shiva wearing the crescent suit many families. Because Mangal rules the star, Murugan worship on Tuesdays is also common, especially in Tamil homes. There is no single rule; choose a form of the divine you can return to steadily, and keep it simple.

ardra-nakshatra.description: Ardra nakshatra, Thiruvathirai in Tamil: Rudra and Rahu, the teardrop, Nataraja's Arudra Darshanam and the Athirampattinam temple, told simply.
outline: Hook: A thunderstorm rolled over Edison the week of Margazhi Thiruvathirai, and I found myself thinking of Rudra, the storm god who weeps, and of the one star he calls his own.

## Ardra nakshatra: storm, tears and Rahu — Rudra as presiding deity and Rahu as adhipati; the teardrop or diamond as symbol, the rain after the storm; tradition describes Thiruvathirai-born people as intense, questioning and capable of starting over after upheaval, a description, not a fate

## Why does Shiva dance on Thiruvathirai? — Ardra as Shiva's own star in Tamil tradition; Arudra Darshanam at Chidambaram on the Margazhi full-moon Thiruvathirai, when Nataraja is brought out at dawn; the sweet Thiruvathirai kali offered that morning; one line from Manikkavasagar's Thiruvempavai, sung through Margazhi

## The star's temple and its monthly day — the Abhaya Varadeeswarar temple at Athirampattinam, near Pattukottai, traditionally associated with the star; a Monday lamp and Rudram or Om Namah Shivaya on the monthly Thiruvathirai day; the yearly star birthday in the birth month, often kept with a Shiva archana
Close: One small thing for this week: after the next storm, or the next hard conversation, sit for five minutes and let it pass through. Rudra's tears are the rain that cleans the air.
takeaways: Ardra, Thiruvathirai in Tamil, is presided over by Rudra with Rahu as its ruling planet; its symbol is a teardrop, the rain after the storm.
Tamil tradition treats Thiruvathirai as Shiva's star, celebrated as Arudra Darshanam for Nataraja in the month of Margazhi.
The Abhaya Varadeeswarar temple at Athirampattinam is traditionally associated with Ardra nakshatra.

faq.q: What is Arudra Darshan and why is it significant?
faq.a: Arudra Darshanam is the festival of Nataraja, Shiva as the cosmic dancer, held on Thiruvathirai star in the Tamil month of Margazhi, usually December or January, near the full moon. At Chidambaram, Nataraja is taken out in procession at dawn. Its significance is the vision of Shiva's dance of creation and release. Homes prepare Thiruvathirai kali, a sweet of rice and jaggery.

faq.q: Which temple is the Thiruvathirai nakshatra temple?
faq.a: The widely cited Tamil list of nakshatra temples names the Abhaya Varadeeswarar temple at Athirampattinam, near Pattukottai in Thanjavur district, as the Thiruvathirai nakshatra temple. Many Thiruvathirai-born devotees also feel a bond with Chidambaram because of Arudra Darshanam. Visiting on the star day, or arranging archana from afar, are both common observances.

faq.q: Is Ardra nakshatra difficult because of Rahu?
faq.a: Jyotish links Ardra with Rudra's storms and Rahu's intensity, so the star is often described as turbulent. The same texts describe it as the star of renewal, the clear air after rain. Tradition's descriptions are not verdicts. Many families simply keep Shiva worship on Mondays and on the star day, and leave the rest to the full chart.

punarvasu-nakshatra.description: Punarvasu nakshatra, Rama's birth star: Aditi and Guru, the quiver of arrows, the story of return from exile, and the Vaniyambadi temple for the star.
outline: Hook: Punarvasu means 'the good returns again', and the prince born under it spent fourteen years proving the name; the story says Rama came home, and the story is really about what it takes to come back.

## Punarvasu nakshatra: Aditi, Jupiter and a quiver — Aditi, mother of the gods and boundless space, as presiding deity and Guru as adhipati; the quiver of arrows as symbol, arrows that are shot and gathered again; tradition describes Punarpoosam-born people as generous, forgiving and resilient, a portrait rather than a promise

## Why is Rama's birth star about returning? — the Valmiki Ramayana's Bala Kanda places Rama's birth under Punarvasu; exile, loss and the return to Ayodhya as the star's arc; Aditi, who bore the gods again after every age, as the same idea told in the sky

## Aditi's temple at Vaniyambadi — the Athitheeswarar temple at Vaniyambadi, whose name recalls Aditi, traditionally associated with the star; Thursday prayers to Guru, a lamp on the monthly star day, and a reading from the Ramayana's return chapters; the yearly star birthday in the birth month as a day to begin again
Close: Every one of us is in some exile: a job lost, a friendship broken, a home left. On your Punarvasu day, take one step back toward something you walked away from.
takeaways: Punarvasu nakshatra is presided over by Aditi, mother of the gods, with Guru (Jupiter) as its ruling planet and a quiver of arrows as its symbol.
The Valmiki Ramayana places Rama's birth under Punarvasu, whose name means the return of the good.
The Athitheeswarar temple at Vaniyambadi is traditionally associated with Punarvasu, called Punarpoosam in Tamil.

The shrine's name recalls Aditi, the star's presiding deity. Punarpoosam-born devotees often visit on their monthly star day, or arrange archana there from a distance.

faq.q: Is Punarvasu the birth star of Rama?
faq.a: Yes. In the Bala Kanda of the Valmiki Ramayana, Rama is described as born when the Moon was in Punarvasu, with Jupiter rising. Ram Navami is kept on the ninth day of the bright fortnight of Chaitra, and this link is why many Punarvasu-born devotees feel a particular closeness to Rama.

faq.q: What are the traits of Punarvasu nakshatra?
faq.a: Tradition describes Punarvasu-born people as generous, forgiving, content with simple things, fond of home and able to bounce back after setbacks. The quiver symbol suggests arrows that return to be used again. These are traditional descriptions linked to the star rather than predictions; the full chart and personal choices shape a person far more.

takeaways: Pushya, Poosam in Tamil, is presided over by Brihaspati with Shani as its ruling planet; its symbol, a cow's udder, stands for nourishment.

faq.q: Why is Shani the lord of Pushya nakshatra if it is so auspicious?
faq.a: In Jyotish, Shani stands for patience, discipline and endurance, not only hardship. Paired with Brihaspati as the presiding deity, the pairing is read as wisdom that ripens slowly and lasts. ## Ashlesha nakshatra: serpents, Mercury and the coil — the Nagas as presiding deities and Budha as adhipati; the coiled serpent as symbol, wisdom held close and energy at rest; tradition describes Ayilyam-born people as perceptive, persuasive and private, a description the star does not force on anyone

## Why do people fear Ayilyam, and should they? — the folk sayings about Ayilyam and in-laws, and why many astrologers, including our family astrologer in Madurai, treat them as custom rather than rule; the Naga as guardian in temple tanks and village shrines; one line from Appar's Thevaram hymn 'we are subject to no one, we fear no death'

## Vrischika rasi: the scorpion and Mars — rasi as the Moon sign in Jyotish; Vrischika as the eighth sign, holding the last quarter of Vishakha and all of Anuradha and Jyeshtha; Mangal as ruler, the Moon debilitated here; the scorpion as intensity and hidden strength; its Western counterpart is Scorpio

## How do you turn intensity into depth? — tradition's portrait of Vrischika: loyal, private, determined, passionate, with suspicion or resentment as the shadow; breath as the first tool: a long exhale before replying to anything that stings

## Vaitheeswaran Koil, Tuesdays and Palani — Vaitheeswaran Koil, the Angaraka shrine among the Navagraha temples; Murugan worship on Tuesdays and at Palani, where Murugan stands as the renunciant who gave up everything; Skanda Sashti as the season of the sign's inner battle
Close: Try this for a week: when something stings, wait three breaths before responding, and on Tuesday light a lamp for Murugan. See what the scorpion does when it is not cornered.
takeaways: Vrischika rasi is the eighth sign in Jyotish, ruled by Mangal (Mars), symbolised by a scorpion; rasi means the Moon sign at birth.
Tradition describes Vrischika natives as loyal, private and intense, with suspicion or resentment as the shadow.
Vaitheeswaran Koil and Murugan temples such as Palani are traditionally linked with Vrischika through its ruling planet.

faq.q: Which god should Vrischika rasi people worship?
faq.a: Because Mangal rules Vrischika, Murugan worship on Tuesdays is the most common practice, especially at Palani and the other abodes of Murugan. Some families visit Vaitheeswaran Koil, the Angaraka shrine among the Navagraha temples. Hanuman and Durga are also popular choices. Tradition offers these as supports; choose one you can return to steadily.

faq.q: What are Vrischika rasi characteristics?
faq.a: Tradition describes people with the Moon in Vrischika as intense, loyal, secretive, determined and emotionally deep, with jealousy, suspicion or holding grudges as possible shadows. The Moon is considered debilitated here, so emotional intensity is often mentioned. These Vrischika rasi characteristics are traditional descriptions, not verdicts; the full chart matters more.

faq.q: Which temple is linked to Viruchigam rasi?
faq.a: Viruchigam, the Tamil name for Vrischika, is traditionally linked with Vaitheeswaran Koil, near Sirkazhi, where Angaraka, Mars, is worshipped among the Navagraha temples. Many families also turn to Murugan at Palani or Tiruchendur. These associations come through the ruling planet rather than a fixed canonical list, and customs vary by region and family.

dhanu-rasi.description: Dhanu rasi explained: Jupiter's archer, the half-horse aiming high, the nature tradition describes, and the Alangudi and Dakshinamurthy link.
outline: Hook: My son, about eleven, tried archery at a summer camp near Edison and came home saying the hard part was not pulling the string but holding still before letting go; that is Dhanu, the archer's sign, in one sentence.

## Dhanu rasi: the archer and Jupiter — rasi as the Moon sign in Jyotish; Dhanu as the ninth sign, holding all of Mula and Purva Ashadha and the first quarter of Uttara Ashadha; Guru as ruler; the archer, half-horse, drawing the bow upward; its Western counterpart is Sagittarius

## Where is the archer aiming? — tradition's portrait of Dhanu: principled, generous, optimistic, fond of learning, travel and teaching, with bluntness or restlessness as the shadow; Arjuna in Drona's archery test, seeing only the bird's eye, as the old picture of focus; the Sun's passage through Dhanu as the month of Margazhi and Andal's Tiruppavai

## Temples and poojas traditionally linked through Guru — Alangudi, the Guru shrine among the Navagraha temples; Thursday prayers to Dakshinamurthy, the silent teacher facing south in Shiva temples; yellow flowers and chickpeas as traditional offerings
Close: One small thing to carry into this week: before your next big decision, hold still for as long as it takes to breathe out fully. Then let go.
takeaways: Dhanu rasi is the ninth sign in Jyotish, ruled by Guru (Jupiter) and symbolised by an archer; rasi means the sign the Moon occupied at birth.
Tradition describes Dhanu natives as principled, generous and optimistic, with bluntness or restlessness as the shadow.
Alangudi, the Guru temple, and Thursday Dakshinamurthy worship are traditionally linked with Dhanu through its ruling planet.

faq.q: Which god should Dhanu rasi people worship?
faq.a: Because Guru rules Dhanu, many families pray to Dakshinamurthy, the teacher form of Shiva, on Thursdays, offering yellow flowers or chickpeas. Some visit Alangudi, the Guru shrine among the Navagraha temples near Kumbakonam. Vishnu worship is also common, especially in Margazhi, when the Sun passes through Dhanu. Keep the practice simple and regular.

faq.q: What are Dhanu rasi characteristics?
faq.a: Tradition describes people with the Moon in Dhanu as honest, generous, idealistic, adventurous and drawn to learning, teaching and faith, with bluntness, overconfidence or restlessness as possible shadows. These Dhanu rasi characteristics come from Guru's rulership and the archer's upward aim. They are traditional descriptions of the Moon sign, not certainties.

faq.q: Which temple is linked to Dhanusu rasi?

These associations come through the ruling planet rather than a fixed canonical list, and customs vary.

makara-rasi.description: Makara rasi explained: the sea-creature makara, Saturn as ruling planet, the slow walker's story, and the Thirunallar temple linked to the sign.
outline: Hook: Shani, the story goes, walks with a limp and is the slowest of the planets; the sign he rules, Makara, is the sign of work that takes as long as it takes.

## What is Makara rasi, and what is a makara? — rasi as the Moon sign in Jyotish; Makara as the tenth sign, holding the last three quarters of Uttara Ashadha, all of Shravana and the first half of Dhanishta; Shani as ruler; the makara, part crocodile, part fish, Ganga's mount and the arch over temple doors; its Western counterpart is Capricorn

## Why does Shani walk so slowly? — the Puranic story of Shani, son of Surya and Chhaya, lamed in a quarrel and forever slow; the story says he is slow because he was hurt, and it is really about patience as a kind of justice; tradition's Makara nature: hardworking, responsible, reserved, patient

## Temples and poojas traditionally linked through Shani — Thirunallar, the Shani shrine among the Navagraha temples, where King Nala is said to have been freed of his long trial; Saturday sesame lamps; Hanuman and Venkateswara worship; Makara Sankranti as the Sun's entry into the sign
Close: The makara in temple arches carries the door on its back without complaint. If your Moon is in Makara, pick one slow task this week and give it an hour a day.
takeaways: Makara rasi is the tenth sign in Jyotish, ruled by Shani (Saturn) and symbolised by the makara, a sea creature; rasi means the Moon sign.
Tradition describes Makara natives as hardworking, responsible and patient, with rigidity or pessimism as the shadow.
Thirunallar, the Shani temple, and Saturday sesame lamps are traditionally linked with Makara through its ruling planet.

faq.q: Which god should Makara rasi people worship?
faq.a: Because Shani rules Makara, many families light sesame oil lamps on Saturdays and pray to Hanuman or Venkateswara. Some visit Thirunallar, the Shani shrine among the Navagraha temples near Karaikal. Tradition sees Shani as the planet of discipline and fairness, so these prayers are offered as devotion and steadiness, not out of fear.

faq.q: What are Makara rasi characteristics?
faq.a: Tradition describes people with the Moon in Makara as disciplined, practical, hardworking, reserved and patient, often succeeding slowly and steadily, with rigidity, worry or pessimism as possible shadows. These Makara rasi characteristics come from Shani's rulership. They are traditional descriptions of the Moon sign rather than predictions; the full chart matters more.

faq.q: Which temple is linked to Makaram rasi?
faq.a: Makaram, the Tamil name for Makara, is traditionally linked with Thirunallar, near Karaikal, where Shani is worshipped among the Navagraha temples and King Nala is said to have ended his long ordeal. Many families also pray at Hanuman temples on Saturdays. These associations come through the ruling planet rather than a fixed canonical list.

kumbha-rasi.description: Kumbha rasi as a practice: Saturn's water-bearer, the pot poured out for others, the nature tradition describes, and the Kumbakonam temple link.
outline: Hook: The water-bearer's pot is only useful when it is poured; Kumbha's practice is giving what you carry, and it starts with noticing how much you hold on to.

## Kumbha rasi in Jyotish: the water-bearer and Saturn — rasi as the Moon sign; Kumbha as the eleventh sign, holding the last half of Dhanishta, all of Shatabhisha and three quarters of Purva Bhadrapada; Shani as ruler; a man carrying an empty pot on his shoulder; its Western counterpart is Aquarius

## Why is the water-bearer's pot empty? — tradition's portrait of Kumbha: humanitarian, independent, inventive, principled, with detachment or stubbornness as the shadow; the Kumbakonam story of the pot of nectar broken by Shiva's arrow after the flood, spilling amrita that made the land holy; the practice: give before you feel full

## Temples and poojas traditionally linked through Shani and the pot — Thirunallar, the Shani shrine among the Navagraha temples; the Adi Kumbeswarar temple at Kumbakonam, named for the pot; Saturday sesame lamps and water offerings; annadhanam as the sign's natural seva
Close: Try this for a week: each day, give one thing away, water to a plant, food to someone, an hour of help. On Saturday, light a sesame lamp and notice how light the pot feels.
takeaways: Kumbha rasi is the eleventh sign in Jyotish, ruled by Shani (Saturn) and symbolised by a water-bearer's pot; rasi means the Moon sign at birth.
Tradition describes Kumbha natives as humanitarian, independent and inventive, with detachment as the shadow.
Thirunallar and the Adi Kumbeswarar temple at Kumbakonam are traditionally linked with Kumbha through its ruler and symbol.

faq.q: Which god should Kumbha rasi people worship?
faq.a: Because Shani rules Kumbha, many families light sesame lamps on Saturdays and pray to Hanuman, Venkateswara or Shiva. Some visit Thirunallar, the Shani shrine among the Navagraha temples, or Adi Kumbeswarar at Kumbakonam, named for the pot. Tradition offers these as supports for a giving, steady life, not as protection from fear.

faq.q: What are Kumbha rasi characteristics?
faq.a: Tradition describes people with the Moon in Kumbha as idealistic, independent, inventive, friendly and devoted to causes larger than themselves, with detachment, stubbornness or aloofness as possible shadows. These Kumbha rasi characteristics come from Shani's rulership and the water-bearer's generosity. They are tradition's descriptions of the Moon sign, not certainties.

faq.q: Which temple is linked to Kumbam rasi?
faq.a: Kumbam, the Tamil name for Kumbha, is traditionally linked with Thirunallar, near Karaikal, where Shani is worshipped among the Navagraha temples. The Adi Kumbeswarar temple at Kumbakonam, whose legend tells of Shiva breaking the pot of nectar, is also associated with the sign's symbol. These links vary by family and region.

## What does it mean to let go? — tradition's portrait of Meena: compassionate, imaginative, spiritual, gentle, with escapism or over-giving as the shadow; Matsya, Vishnu's fish avatar who carried Manu's boat through the flood; one line from the Bhagavad Gita on offering the fruit of action and being free

## Temples and poojas traditionally linked through Guru and the fish — Alangudi, the Guru shrine among the Navagraha temples; Thursday Dakshinamurthy prayers; Madurai Meenakshi, the fish-eyed goddess, whom many Meena families feel drawn to as a folk association rather than a rule
Close: One small thing to carry into this week: at the end of each day, say one sentence of thanks and let the rest go. The fish do not carry the river.
takeaways: Meena rasi is the twelfth and last sign in Jyotish, ruled by Guru (Jupiter) and symbolised by two fish; rasi means the Moon sign at birth.
Tradition describes Meena natives as compassionate, imaginative and spiritual, with escapism or over-giving as the shadow.
Alangudi, the Guru temple, and Thursday Dakshinamurthy prayers are traditionally linked with Meena through its ruling planet.

faq.q: Which god should Meena rasi people worship?
faq.a: Because Guru rules Meena, many families pray to Dakshinamurthy on Thursdays and some visit Alangudi, the Guru shrine among the Navagraha temples. Vishnu, remembered as Matsya the fish avatar, is a natural choice, and many feel drawn to Meenakshi at Madurai. Tradition offers these as supports, not obligations; a steady practice matters most.

faq.q: What are Meena rasi characteristics?
faq.a: Tradition describes people with the Moon in Meena as compassionate, intuitive, creative, gentle and spiritually inclined, with escapism, indecision or giving too much as possible shadows. These Meena rasi characteristics come from Guru's rulership and the two fish. They are traditional descriptions of the Moon sign rather than predictions; the full chart matters more.

faq.q: Which temple is linked to Meenam rasi?
faq.a: Meenam, the Tamil name for Meena, is traditionally linked with Alangudi, near Kumbakonam, where Guru is worshipped among the Navagraha temples. Many Meenam families also feel a bond with the Meenakshi temple at Madurai because of the fish in the goddess's name. That second link is a folk association rather than a rule, and customs vary.
